text.p: W.R. Grace & Co., a maker of speciality chemicals and packaging, Tuesday reported a smaller fourth-quarter loss amid charges from divested businesses and asbestos-related legal costs.
The company also said it expects to have higher profits in 1997.
Grace said the fourth-quarter loss was $56.8 million, or 70 cents a share, compared with a loss of $473.8 million, or $4.87 a share, a year earlier.
Sales fell to $863 million from $934.1 million a year earlier.
During the quarter the company recorded special charges of $283 million, related primarily to anticipated future asbestos personal injury litigation and settlement costs and restructuring.

"The new Grace is now focused on profitably growing our three core businesses of packaging, catalyst and silica products and construction products," Grace Chairman Albert J. Costello said in a statement.

"We expect to deliver higher profits and cash flow in 1997, as we continue to reduce expenses and capital spending, and to build on our global market leadership positions in each of our businesses," he said.

For the year, Grace earned $2.86 billion, $2.32 a share, before a gain from the discontinued health care segment and the disposition of other businesses. A year earlier Grace lost $325.94 million, or $1.87 a share. Sales were $3.49 billion, compared with $3.59 billion in 1995.
Grace's stock slipped 37.5 cents to $50.50 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
